description: Small team, big ideas, limitless possibilities!
summary: This project explores how space telescopes help scientists observe and understand the universe. It focuses on two famous space telescopes: the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope. Hubble captures images using visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light, while James Webb mainly observes infrared light. These telescopes help scientists study distant galaxies, stars, planets and the early universe. Through this project, students can discover how technology helps us explore the mysteries of space.
details: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched on 24 April 1990 to observe the universe from above Earth's atmosphere. Hubble captures amazing images of galaxies, stars and planets using visible, ultraviolet and near-infrared light. The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on 25 December 2021 and is designed to observe the universe mainly using infrared light. Webb helps scientists study the first galaxies, the formation of stars and distant planets beyond our solar system. Together, Hubble and Webb help scientists discover new information about space and understand how our universe has changed over time.
